description: Golden dataset for the customer support email classifier. Each case has a human-verified category and ideal one-sentence summary.

changelog.change: Initial 60 cases: 15 per category, including all 22 hard edge cases. IDs are stable, so gaps in numbering are expected.

cases.input: Hi, I was charged twice for my Pro subscription this month. Can you refund one of the charges?

expected.summary: Customer was double-charged for their Pro subscription and wants one charge refunded.

cases.notes: Classic duplicate charge; baseline billing case.

cases.input: Could you send me the invoice for last month? Our finance team needs it with our company VAT number on it.

expected.summary: Customer needs last month's invoice with their company VAT number for their finance team.

cases.notes: Invoice request.

cases.input: I cancelled my free trial two days before it ended but I still got charged $19.99. Please reverse this.

expected.summary: Customer was charged after cancelling their free trial and wants the charge reversed.

cases.notes: Mentions cancelling, which can pull toward account, but the problem is the charge.

cases.input: What's the price difference between the monthly and annual plans? Is there a discount for paying yearly?

expected.summary: Customer asks how monthly and annual pricing compare and whether yearly billing is discounted.

cases.notes: Pricing question.

cases.input: My card expires next week. How do I update my payment method so my plan doesn't lapse?

expected.summary: Customer wants to update their payment card before it expires so their plan continues.

cases.notes: Payment details live in settings, so this can look like an account question.

cases.input: I upgraded to the Business plan in the middle of the month. Why is my bill so much higher than the plan price?

expected.summary: Customer is confused about why their bill is higher than the plan price after a mid-month upgrade.

cases.notes: Proration confusion; the model must recognize an unexpected amount as billing.

cases.input: Please cancel my renewal. I don't want to be charged again next month, but I'd like to keep using it until the current period ends.

expected.summary: Customer wants to cancel their renewal to avoid future charges while keeping access until the period ends.

cases.notes: Subscription cancellation is about charges, but it could be read as an account request.

cases.input: The dashboard won't load. It just shows a spinning wheel forever. I've tried both Chrome and Safari.

expected.summary: The dashboard is stuck loading in both Chrome and Safari.

cases.notes: Clear loading bug; baseline technical case.

cases.input: Every time I click 'Export to PDF' the app crashes and closes. I'm on version 4.2 on Windows 11.

expected.summary: The app crashes when the customer exports to PDF on version 4.2 on Windows 11.

cases.notes: Crash with version details.

cases.input: I'm getting 'Error 502 Bad Gateway' when I try to open any project. Is something down on your end?

expected.summary: Customer gets a 502 error when opening projects and asks whether there's an outage.

cases.notes: Error code plus outage question.

cases.input: How do I connect the app to Google Calendar? I can't find the integration anywhere in the settings.

expected.summary: Customer can't find how to connect the app to Google Calendar.

cases.notes: How-to question; mentioning settings can pull toward account.

cases.input: Push notifications stopped working on my Android phone after yesterday's update.

expected.summary: Push notifications stopped working on the customer's Android phone after the latest update.

cases.notes: Regression after an update.

cases.input: Your API keeps returning 429 errors even though we're way under the rate limit for our plan.

expected.summary: The API returns 429 rate-limit errors even though the customer is under their plan's limit.

cases.notes: Mentions the plan, which can pull toward billing, but the problem is API behavior.

cases.input: Is there a way to work offline? I travel a lot and lose connection on flights.

expected.summary: Customer asks whether the app can be used offline while traveling.

cases.notes: Feature question that could be mistaken for general.

cases.input: I can't log in. It says my account is locked after too many failed attempts.

expected.summary: Customer's account is locked after too many failed login attempts.

cases.notes: Locked account; baseline account case.

cases.input: How do I change the email address on my account? I'm leaving my job and will lose access to my work inbox.

expected.summary: Customer wants to change their account email because they'll lose access to their work inbox.

cases.notes: Profile change.

cases.input: I never got the password reset email. I've checked my spam folder and waited over an hour.

expected.summary: Customer hasn't received a password reset email despite checking spam and waiting an hour.

cases.notes: Email delivery problem could look technical, but it's about getting into the account.

cases.input: Please delete my account and all of my personal data.

expected.summary: Customer wants their account and all personal data deleted.

cases.notes: Account deletion request.

cases.input: I'd like to add two new teammates to our workspace and give one of them admin rights.

expected.summary: Customer wants to add two teammates to their workspace and make one an admin.

cases.notes: User management.

cases.input: Can I change my username? I made a typo when I signed up.

expected.summary: Customer wants to change their username to fix a typo from sign-up.

cases.notes: Profile change.

cases.input: I got a login alert from a device in another country. I didn't sign in from there. What should I do?

expected.summary: Customer received a login alert from an unfamiliar foreign device and wants to know what to do.

cases.notes: Security concern with an urgent tone.

cases.input: I'm not receiving my two-factor codes by SMS anymore, so I'm stuck at the login screen.

expected.summary: Customer can't log in because they're no longer receiving two-factor codes by SMS.

cases.notes: Code delivery could be read as technical, but the impact is account access.

cases.input: How do I turn off the marketing emails? I only want important account notifications.

expected.summary: Customer wants to stop marketing emails while keeping important account notifications.

cases.notes: Notification preferences could be read as general.

cases.input: Do you have any openings for remote designers? I'd love to work with your team.

expected.summary: Customer asks about remote designer job openings.

cases.notes: Job inquiry; baseline general case.

cases.input: Just wanted to say your support team was fantastic last week. Thanks, Maria!

expected.summary: Customer is thanking the support team for great help last week.

cases.notes: Positive feedback with no request.

cases.input: Are you planning to release a Linux version of the desktop app?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether a Linux version of the desktop app is planned.

cases.notes: Roadmap question; mentioning a platform can pull toward technical.

cases.input: What are your support hours over the holidays?

expected.summary: Customer asks about support hours during the holidays.

cases.notes: Support availability question.

cases.input: I'm writing a blog post comparing productivity tools. Could someone from your team answer a few questions?

expected.summary: Customer is writing a blog post and wants to interview someone from the team.

cases.notes: Press or media request.

cases.input: Can I visit your office? I'll be in Berlin next month and would love to say hello.

expected.summary: Customer asks whether they can visit the office while in Berlin next month.

cases.notes: Office visit request.

cases.input: Do you have a partner or affiliate program? I run a consulting business and recommend tools to my clients.

expected.summary: Customer asks about a partner or affiliate program for their consulting business.

cases.notes: Partnership inquiry.

cases.input: refund??

expected.summary: Customer is asking for a refund without giving details.

cases.notes: Extremely short; one word of signal.

cases.input: cant login

expected.summary: Customer can't log in.

cases.notes: Extremely short with a typo.

cases.input: app broken

expected.summary: Customer reports the app is broken without details.

cases.notes: Extremely short and vague.

cases.input: helo, i tryed to pay my invoce 3 times and the card keeps geting declind, wat is wrong??

expected.summary: Customer's card keeps getting declined when they try to pay an invoice.

cases.notes: Heavy typos; a failing payment could also look technical.

cases.input: my pasword reset link sayz expired evry time i click it rite away

expected.summary: Customer's password reset link shows as expired even when clicked immediately.

cases.notes: Typos; arguably a bug (technical), labeled account because the outcome is being locked out.

cases.input: Hola, I was charged dos veces este mes for my subscription. ¿Me pueden devolver uno?

expected.summary: Customer was charged twice this month and asks for one charge to be refunded.

cases.notes: Spanish and English mixed.

cases.input: Bonjour, l'application plante every time I open the camera feature. Merci de m'aider.

expected.summary: The app crashes whenever the customer opens the camera feature.

cases.notes: French and English mixed.

cases.input: Wow, love paying for a "premium" plan that's been down three times this week. Really getting my money's worth.

expected.summary: Customer sarcastically complains that the service has been down three times this week despite paying for premium.

cases.notes: Sarcasm; mentions paying, but the core issue is outages.

cases.input: Great, another password reset email that never arrives. Fifth time's the charm, right?

expected.summary: Customer sarcastically reports that password reset emails keep failing to arrive.

cases.notes: Sarcasm plus repeated failed attempts.

cases.input: I was charged for the Pro plan but my account still shows the Free plan and I can't use any Pro features.

expected.summary: Customer paid for the Pro plan but their account still shows Free and Pro features don't work.

cases.notes: Could be billing, account, or technical; labeled billing because the customer paid for something they didn't receive.

cases.input: I want to close my account. Also, will I get a refund for the rest of the year since I paid annually?

expected.summary: Customer wants to close their account and asks about a refund for the unused part of their annual plan.

cases.notes: Two intents (account closure and refund); labeled billing because the refund needs a decision.

cases.input: Is my data safe with you? I read about a breach at another company and got worried.

expected.summary: Customer is worried about data security after reading about another company's breach.

cases.notes: Security worry with no specific account problem; could be read as account.

cases.input: The mobile app logs me out every time I close it, so I have to sign in again each time.

expected.summary: The mobile app logs the customer out every time they close it.

cases.notes: Mentions signing in, but it's a session bug, not an access problem.

cases.input: The dark mode setting doesn't stick. It switches back to light mode every time I restart the app.

expected.summary: The dark mode setting resets to light mode whenever the app restarts.

cases.notes: Mentions a setting, which can pull toward account.

cases.input: Our SSO login through Okta started failing this morning with an 'invalid SAML response' error.

expected.summary: SSO login through Okta has been failing since this morning with an invalid SAML response error.

cases.notes: Login failure caused by an integration error; labeled technical because the error points to the SSO setup, not the user's credentials.

cases.input: Can I have two separate workspaces under one login, one for work and one for personal stuff?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether one login can hold separate work and personal workspaces.

cases.notes: Account structure question.

cases.input: I signed up with Google, but now I want to log in with a regular email and password instead.

expected.summary: Customer signed up with Google and wants to switch to email and password login.

cases.notes: Login method change.

cases.input: Do you have a status page where I can check for outages?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether there's a status page for checking outages.

cases.notes: Mentions outages, but asks for a resource rather than reporting a problem.

cases.input: Who should I contact about a security vulnerability I found on your website?

expected.summary: Customer wants to know who to contact about a security vulnerability they found.

cases.notes: Security topic that could be read as technical.

cases.input: Could we book a demo for my team of 40 people sometime next week?

expected.summary: Customer wants to book a demo for their 40-person team next week.

cases.notes: Sales request that could be read as billing.

cases.input: Feature suggestion: a calendar view for tasks would be amazing.

expected.summary: Customer suggests adding a calendar view for tasks.

cases.notes: Feature request that could be read as technical.

cases.input: thx!

expected.summary: Customer is saying thanks.

cases.notes: Extremely short with no request.

cases.input: invoice pls

expected.summary: Customer is asking for an invoice.

cases.notes: Extremely short.

cases.input: wen i clik save it sais erorr and nothin hapens

expected.summary: Customer gets an error and nothing happens when they click save.

cases.notes: Heavy typos.

cases.input: Hallo, ich kann mich nicht einloggen since I changed my phone. Bitte helfen!

expected.summary: Customer can't log in since changing their phone and is asking for help.

cases.notes: German and English mixed; likely two-factor tied to the old phone.

cases.input: Bonjour ! Est-ce que vous avez des offres d'emploi in London?

expected.summary: Customer asks whether there are job openings in London.

cases.notes: French and English mixed.

cases.input: Oh fantastic, charged again after I cancelled. Third time now. You guys are amazing at taking money.

expected.summary: Customer sarcastically complains about being charged after cancelling, for the third time.

cases.notes: Sarcasm plus a repeated billing failure.

cases.input: Thanks for the 'quick' reply. It only took two weeks.

expected.summary: Customer sarcastically complains that support took two weeks to reply.

cases.notes: Sarcastic complaint about support speed, with no product issue; easily misread as thanks.

cases.input: After the update I can't see any of my old projects. Did my account get reset?

expected.summary: Customer's old projects disappeared after an update and they suspect their account was reset.

cases.notes: Customer suspects an account problem, but missing data after an update points to a bug.

cases.input: We're thinking about switching from your competitor. Can you match their price and help us move our data over?

expected.summary: Customer is considering switching from a competitor and asks for a price match and help migrating data.

cases.notes: Mixes a pricing request with a migration question; labeled billing because the price is the deciding question.
